issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 exhibits two internal mathematical contradictions in its line search and update rules. First, lines 7-13 evaluate the Armijo condition strictly along the descent direction $-D^{(j)}$ (testing candidate points $\Pi_E(\varepsilon^{(j)} - \tau D^{(j)})$), but line 15 updates the control along the opposite direction $+D^{(j)}$ ($\varepsilon^{(j+1)} \gets \Pi_E(\varepsilon^{(j)} + \sigma^{(j+1)} D^{(j)})$), negating the descent guarantee verified by the line search. Second, in the forward expansion branch (lines 12-14), the loop continues while the Armijo condition holds; when the while loop exits, $\tau^{(k)}$ is precisely the first step size that violates the Armijo condition, yet line 14 sets $\sigma^{(j+1)} \gets \tau^{(k)}$ rather than the last valid step $\tau^{(k-1)}$ (or $b\tau^{(k)}$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign in line 15 to $-\sigma^{(j+1)} D^{(j)}$ (or test $+D^{(j)}$ throughout lines 7-13) and set $\sigma^{(j+1)} \gets b\tau^{(k)}$ (or $\tau^{(k-1)}$) upon exiting the forward while loop in line 14.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 fails to guarantee descent or convergence; execution can take steps in the ascent direction or adopt step sizes known to violate the Armijo criterion.
issues.title: Direction contradiction and invalid step selection in DAL line search
issues.why_classification: A routine, local correction to the signs and step index restores the standard two-way Armijo projected gradient scheme without altering results or requiring new proofs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:existence1}, it is immediate to show coercivity in the primal variables, ensuring that the minimum is attained in a weakly compact set. The ensemble of these properties is sufficient to guarantee the existence of a saddle point in our setting (see for instance \cite[Chapter VI]{ET_1999}) and strong duality is directly implied by it.

In general, the saddle point is not unique. In fact, when approaching the minimum point $(u^*,v^*)$ in the primal variables (which is unique), the term $\int_\Omega \mu \cdot (v^*-\nabla u^*)$ vanishes, so that any $\mu \in L^2(\Omega; \R^2)$ becomes feasible.

issues.failure_explanation:
Theorem 4.1 claims the existence of a saddle point $(u^*, v^*, \mu^*)$ for $L$ in $H^1(\Omega) 	imes L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) 	imes L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ and strong duality. This is mathematically false: if a saddle point existed, $v^* = 
abla u^*$ and $u^* \in H^1(\Omega)$ would be a minimizer of the TV/ROF functional $K(u)$. For general images $I$ with sharp edges, minimizers of the ROF functional do not belong to $H^1(\Omega)$ but strictly to $BV(\Omega) \setminus H^1(\Omega)$ (as shown in Chambolle & Lions 1997), so the infimum over $H^1(\Omega)$ is not attained. Furthermore, the proof's claim of coercivity in the primal variables fails: on the subspace $v = 
abla u$, $L(u, 
abla u, \mu) = \int_\Omega |
abla u| +  rac{\alpha}{2}(u-I)^2\,dx$, which only controls the $L^1$ norm of $
abla u$ and allows $\|u\|_{H^1} 	o \infty$ on bounded sequences of $L$. Finally, Ekeland-Temam minimax theorems require compactness or coercivity in the dual variable, whereas $L$ is linear in $\mu$ on the unbounded space $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$. The subsequent prose assertion that 'any $\mu \in L^2$ becomes feasible' at the saddle point is likewise false, as the saddle point requires $\mu^* \in -\partial|v^*|$ and $-\dive \mu^* + \alpha(u^*-I) = 0$.

failure_location.quote: There exists a saddle point for the functional $L : H^1(\Omega) 	imes L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) 	imes L^2(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) \to \R$ defined in \eqref{eq:cost_tv_regular}. In particular, the strong duality condition holds:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the saddle-point problem and duality theorem in a discrete setting on the pixel grid (where finite-dimensional spaces guarantee existence and qualification), or in $BV(\Omega)$ using an appropriate dual space and relaxation.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical foundation of the TV saddle-point formulation and the guarantee of zero duality gap for the continuous problem fail.
issues.title: Non-existence of saddle point and false coercivity for regularized TV functional
issues.why_classification: Resolving the issue in the continuous setting requires rebuilding the functional framework in $BV(\Omega)$ or retreating entirely to the finite-dimensional discrete formulation, abandoning the continuous $H^1$ saddle-point theorem.
